title: Finite Postnikov propagation of invertibility
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ and cohomology functors $H^q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $\Phi,\Psi:D^+(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$ be exact triangulated functors on the full bounded-below derived category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], with specified shift isomorphisms $\xi_M:\Phi(M[1])\cong\Phi(M)[1]$ and $\zeta_M:\Psi(M[1])\cong\Psi(M)[1]$. Let $\eta:\Phi\to\Psi$ be a natural transformation satisfying $\zeta_M\eta_{M[1]}=\eta_M[1]\xi_M$. For $E\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ let $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $a-1\le b$ and $H^q(E)=0$ for $q<a$. Suppose $\eta_{H^q(E)[0]}$ is invertible for every $a\le q\le b$, where $H^q(E)[0]$ denotes the cohomology object placed in degree zero. Then $\eta_{\tau_{\le b}E}$ is invertible, with canonical upper truncation from [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. This includes the empty interval $b=a-1$.

proof.text: Let t be the standard t-structure induced on D+(A). The lower cohomology vanishing hypothesis gives E >= a using DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and Plus.isGE_ι_obj_iff. Work directly with t.truncLE, so no choice of a concrete cochain-complex representative or comparison with concrete truncations is needed.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), realized using the induced t-structure and the proved derived-category API

proof.text: The degree-one shift equation expresses eta at M[1] as the composite of the specified shift isomorphisms with eta(M)[1]. Therefore eta(M[1]) is invertible if and only if eta(M) is: shift by one reflects isomorphisms. Integer induction about zero, using shiftFunctorZero and shiftFunctorAdd, gives invertibility at M[n] for every integer n whenever it holds at M. Naturality transports invertibility along every object isomorphism (NatTrans.isIso_app_iff_of_iso).

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), realized using the induced t-structure and the proved derived-category API

proof.text: For the base q=a-1, t.isZero_truncLE_obj_of_isGE shows that t.truncLE(q)(E) is zero. The exact functors are additive and preserve zero objects, so eta at this object is a morphism between two zero objects and is invertible. This also proves the empty-interval case without any use of the cohomology-component hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), realized using the induced t-structure and the proved derived-category API

proof.text: For a-1 <= q and q+1 <= b, put X=t.truncLE(q+1)(E) and apply the standard distinguished triangle t.truncLE(q)(X) -> X -> t.truncGE(q+1)(X) -> t.truncLE(q)(X)[1]. The truncation of the inclusion X -> E is an isomorphism in degrees <= q, by t.isIso_truncLE_map_truncLEι_app, so the induction hypothesis transports to the first vertex. The proved theorem DerivedCategory.Plus.nonempty_eTruncGE_eTruncLT_iso_singleFunctor identifies the third vertex with H^(q+1)(E) in degree q+1. The singleFunctors.shiftIso identifies this with H^(q+1)(E)[0][-(q+1)], where the preceding shift argument and the cohomology-component hypothesis give invertibility.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), realized using the induced t-structure and the proved derived-category API

proof.text: Apply both exact functors to that distinguished triangle. Construct their triangle morphism with the components of eta: the first two squares are naturality and the last is naturality composed with the given degree-one shift equation. Mathlib Pretriangulated.isIso₂_of_isIso₁₃ gives invertibility at X from the first and third components. Integer induction from a-1 to b completes the proof. This direct construction uses only the stated degree-one equation and does not require constructing a NatTrans.CommShift instance in every integer degree.
